notes: Optional components (breadboard, VL53L0X/ultrasonic sensor, line sensors) are only mentioned as future additions with no wiring in this tutorial, so they are omitted.

The motor controller board is not in the catalogue, so it is a new type. The GPIO header is a single port and the 26-pin push-on is modelled as one edge; GPIO 7/8/9/10 are not modelled as separate pins.
The wheel is also a new type, with one axle-hole port 'hub'. dc-motor has no axle port, so the wheel-to-motor edge has no motor port.
The battery holder's red wire goes to + and its black wire to -. The wires are integral to the pack, so they are modelled as pack ports connected straight to the screw terminals.

The motor wires are modelled as jumper-wire parts soldered to the motor terminals and screwed into terminal blocks A and B. Which wire goes to which terminal does not matter. The motors are on terminal blocks A and B, but which motor is left or right is set in software.
The batteries sit in the holder with no port-specific edges because the pack has only positive and negative ports.
The power bank to Pi USB-C link is shown directly because no cable is in the parts list.
Solder and electrical tape are shared single parts. The tape is optional and is used to protect the soldered joints. The solder is only needed if the motors have no wires attached.
Motors are fixed in the box with putty or tape, which is not in the parts list. The wheels attach to the axles through the box walls.
